question: Is the MEMORY rollback journal (connection.rs:1-48) the cost inside the 60.3% database term?
method: Same synthetic replica and preamble as cadence-calibration.json; 8,192 transactions of one 32 KiB row each, 268,435,456 bytes in every arm; only PRAGMA journal_mode varies. synchronous stays OFF.
verdict: REFUTED. MEMORY is 0.927x OFF - i.e. measured slightly FASTER than no journal at all, so the in-memory rollback journal costs nothing at this shape. DELETE (a real on-disk rollback journal) is 4.01x slower, which is a statement about disk journaling, not about this product: the product does not use DELETE and must not be moved to OFF, which would remove the runtime rollback atomicity connection.rs:3-7 retains.
caveat: One sample per arm, synthetic replica, one table.
